1. Admission & Registration Guidelines 
Purpose: This section outlines the entry requirements, required documentation, and step-by-step 
registration procedure for new and returning students. 
Admission Requirements 
 High School Certificate: Applicants must present an original, recognized High School 
Certificate (or equivalent) certified by the Ministry of Education, with a minimum 
passing grade of 60% (or equivalent grade boundary based on faculty). 
 Identification & Photos: 4 recent passport-size photographs along with a valid copy of a 
National ID Card or Passport. 
 Character Reference: A formal letter of recommendation or character reference from 
the student's previous secondary school or employer. 
 Entrance Examination: Candidates applying for specific competitive faculties (e.g., 
Medicine, Engineering) or scholarship schemes must sit for the University Entrance 
Examination (evaluating English Proficiency and Mathematics). 
Registration Steps

Examination (evaluating English Proficiency and Mathematics). 
Registration Steps 
1. Application Submission: Fill out and submit the official application form via the online 
student portal or at the Admissions Office on campus. 
2. Document Verification: The Registrar's Office reviews and authenticates all submitted 
credentials. 
3. Application Fee Payment: Pay a non-refundable application fee of $20 to process the 
credentials. 
4. Student ID & LMS Activation: Upon payment and approval, students receive an 
official Student ID Number and access credentials for the Learning Management System 
(LMS). 
2. Tuition & Financial Fee Structure 
Purpose: Provides complete financial transparency regarding tuition rates, payment schedules, 
and institutional financial policies. 
Detailed Fee Breakdown

Fee Category Amount ($ 
USD) Payment Due Date 
Application Fee $20 One-time (Upon application submission) 
Semester Registration 
Fee $50 Due at the beginning of each semester 
Monthly Tuition Fee $50 – $120 Monthly or per semester (Varies by 
faculty) 
Laboratory / Practical 
Fee $30 – $50 Per semester (Engineering & Health 
Sciences) 
Financial Policies & Regulations 
 Payment Deadlines: Monthly tuition fees must be settled by the 5th of every month. 
Semester fees must be cleared prior to the start of the academic term. 
 Late Payment Consequences: Students with outstanding balances beyond the grace 
period may face restricted access to mid-term or final examinations, as well as portal 
lockouts. 
 Payment Methods: All financial transactions must be processed through the university's 
official bank accounts or authorized mobile money services (Zaad, Sahal, EVC Plus). 
Physical cash is not accepted at the Finance Office; deposit receipts must be submitted 
for reconciliation.

3. Faculties & Academic Programs 
Purpose: Highlights the primary academic divisions, degree offerings, and program scopes 
available at the university. 
1. Faculty of Health Sciences

 Programs Offered: Bachelor of Medicine & General Surgery (6 Years), Bachelor of 
Science in Nursing (4 Years), Bachelor of Public Health (4 Years), Bachelor of Medical 
Laboratory Sciences (4 Years). 
 Overview: Designed to train skilled healthcare professionals through rigorous clinical 
coursework, state-of-the-art laboratory work, and hospital internships. 
2. Faculty of Engineering & Information Technology 
 Programs Offered: B.Sc. in Computer Science, B.Sc. in Software Engineering, B.Sc. in 
Civil Engineering, B.Sc. in Information Technology. 
 Overview: Focuses on modern technology, software design, infrastructure development, 
and practical engineering skills tailored to local and international job markets. 
3. Faculty of Economics & Management Science 
 Programs Offered: Bachelor of Business Administration, B.Sc. in Accounting & 
Finance, B.A. in Economics, Bachelor of Public Administration.

 Programs Offered: Bachelor of Business Administration, B.Sc. in Accounting & 
Finance, B.A. in Economics, Bachelor of Public Administration. 
 Overview: Prepares students for leadership roles in commerce, financial analysis, 
organizational management, and public sector governance. 
4. Academic Schedules & Study Shifts 
Purpose: Details the available learning schedules, shift options, and the general academic 
calendar. 
Study Shifts 
 Morning Shift: 7:30 AM – 12:00 PM (Saturday to Wednesday) 
 Afternoon Shift: 1:30 PM – 5:00 PM (Saturday to Wednesday) 
 Evening Shift: 5:30 PM – 8:30 PM (Tailored for working professionals) 
Academic Calendar Overview 
Fall Semester: 
 Registration Opens: September 1st 
 Classes Begin: October 1st 
 Mid-Term Examinations: November 15th – 20th 
 Final Examinations: January 20th – 31st 
Spring Semester: 
 Classes Begin: February 15th 
 Mid-Term Examinations: April 10th – 15th 
 Final Examinations: June 15th – 25th
